FL-4512 · measured on the raster, not typed

Seam Ledger

Every glyph pair here was placed at its real offset on the unifont cell and measured: seam gap in pixels, port contact, and DSM. Rasters are the measured pixels, drawn 1:2 as the cell is.

DSM is Xu 2017’s structure-map distance (Eq. 19) between two rasters: every ink pixel looks for a partner within 5 px and pays for the difference in edge strength and stroke angle, in both directions. 0 means the composite matches the reference stroke pixel for pixel; lower reads more like one continuous stroke. It is an offline authoring number, not a runtime term.

Stacked over |the anti-aliasing family, ranked by distance from a continuous bar

Reference is the box-drawing bar │ over itself: a 0 px seam, outside the plate alphabet. Inside the plate alphabet only four pairs close their seam (,‾ |‾ {‾ }‾, all with the overline below). The amber line is the cell seam.

The nine authored combinationsglyph_combinations.v1.json

Unifont’s | spans rows 2–15, so it is terminal (bottom contact only), not through-vertical; _ sits on row 14, one row above the floor. Both are measured facts of this font, not authoring errors.
